newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans flat '97 beet output of 24 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans flat '97 beet output of 24 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine plans its 1997 output of sugar beet to be flat on last year's 24 million tonnes despite plans to sow a smaller area, a senior official from Ukraine's Sugar Research Institute said on Tuesday.

"Obviously at this time no one can give a precise forecast on the future beet harvest, but one thing is clear -- Ukraine plans to maintain last year's crop," Leonid Bershtein, a deputy director at the institute, told Reuters.
According to Agriculture Ministry data, the former Soviet republic plans to sow 1.35 million hectares with sugar beets this spring -- down from 1.41 million hectares in 1996 and 1995.
But Bershtein said Ukraine was also counting on better weather, after a drought at the start of last year's growing season ruined hopes for a 30 million-tonne sugar beet harvest.
The Agriculture Ministry and agricultural experts said that this year the soil had enough moisture to produce favourable conditions for growth.
The government has promised farmers more fertilisers and pesticides than in 1996, but the farm sector continues to suffer from shortages.
Ukraine requires about 1.40 million tonnes of refined whites to meet domestic demand and produced 2.70 million tonnes of whites from last year's beet harvest.
Russia, traditionally a large export market for Ukraine, has said it plans to impose a quota of 1.15 million tonnes on Ukrainian sugar to prevent what it calls dumping on its market.
Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said last week that Ukraine had 900,000 tonnes of sugar left over from the 1996-97 harvest.
While there were enough seeds for the spring sowing campaign, a lack of modern machinery and parts was particularly worrisome, Bershtein said. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev newsroom, +380 44 229 2264
